March 15, 2018 - By Louis Casey 
Advanced Emissions Solutions, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides clean coal technology and the associated specialty chemicals serving the coal-fueled power plant industry in the United States. The company has market cap of $225.87 million. It operates in two divisions, Refined Coal and Emissions Control. It has a 8.3 P/E ratio. The firm offers Activated Carbon Injection systems to reduce mercury emissions over a range of plant configurations and coal types; Dry Sorbent Injection (DSI) systems to reduce emissions of sulfur dioxide and other acid gases, such as sulfur trioxide and hydrogen chloride; and ADAir-Mixer that alters flue gas flow to enhance mixing and optimize particle dispersion to reduce sorbent consumption for DSI and ACI systems. 
Greenlight Capital Inc increased Mylan N V (MYL) stake by 0.4% reported in 2017Q3 SEC filing. Greenlight Capital Inc acquired 42,600 shares as Mylan N V (MYL)’s stock declined 9.77%. The Greenlight Capital Inc holds 10.74 million shares with $337.05 million value, up from 10.70 million last quarter. Mylan N V now has $21.45 billion valuation. The stock decreased 0.83% or $0.35 during the last trading session, reaching $41.67. About 2.22M shares traded. Mylan N.V. (NASDAQ:MYL) has declined 7.73% since March 15, 2017 and is downtrending. It has underperformed by 24.43% the S&P500. 
Greenlight Capital Inc decreased Amerco (NASDAQ:UHAL) stake by 170,000 shares to 50,000 valued at $18.75M in 2017Q3. It also reduced Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL) stake by 1.74 million shares and now owns 2.19M shares. Rite Aid Corp (NYSE:RAD) was reduced too.

Mizuho initiated it with “Buy” rating and $49 target in Wednesday, October 26 report. The firm earned “Buy” rating on Tuesday, February 6 by BMO Capital Markets. The firm has “Outperform” rating by Leerink Swann given on Saturday, August 29. Citigroup upgraded Mylan N.V. (NASDAQ:MYL) on Friday, November 13 to “Buy” rating. On Wednesday, October 4 the stock rating was maintained by Cowen & Co with “Hold”.
